Axis num:
- Register: "R049/2006-FR2-2008.02 Rev. 3"
- Document: "2006-FR2-08.02"

The register has the full OIML certificate number format: R049/2006-FR2-2008.02 Rev. 3. The document shows "2006-FR2-08.02" — this looks like a truncated/abbreviated form of the same certificate number (2006-FR2-2008.02, with the "20" in "2008" possibly truncated to "08"). This is a number format difference that clearly denotes the same certificate — same-entity, best_value = register's canonical form "R049/2006-FR2-2008.02 Rev. 3".

Axis applicant:
- Register: "CONTAZARA S.A"
- Document: "CONTAZARA"

This is legal-suffix drift — "S.A" is the legal suffix (Société Anonyme). Same entity, same-entity verdict, best_value should be... The rule says legal-suffix drift = same-entity. What's the best value? The register has "CONTAZARA S.A" which is more complete. The rules say for same-entity from number/year format differences, use register's canonical form. For same-entity generally, the fused record should carry the more complete/canonical form — the register's "CONTAZARA S.A" is fuller and consistent with the certificate issuer context (Contazara S.A. is a French company). Actually, the document is the legal instrument, but the document value here is just less complete ("CONTAZARA" vs "CONTAZARA S.A"). The fuller form includes the suffix; it's likely the register's form is the better canonical. Best value = "CONTAZARA S.A".

Wait — should best_value for same-entity applicant be document's since certificate is legal instrument? The rule only specifies best_value = document's for different-entity. For same-entity, no explicit rule except for number format (register canonical). For applicant same-entity, the register's form is a superset — includes legal suffix. So best_value = "CONTAZARA S.A".
